LineageEdgeAnswer.description: One way an input influences an output of the job.

input_column.description: For a column edge, the input column; for a parameter edge, the parameter name such as @AsOfDate; else null.
input_column.title: Input Column

input_kind.description: column: a column of one of the job's input tables; parameter: a job parameter such as @AsOfDate; constant: a literal in the code; generated: a value the engine makes, such as an IDENTITY key or a load timestamp.
input_kind.title: Input Kind

input_table.description: For a column edge, the job INPUT table it belongs to, schema-qualified (trace through temp tables and work data sets back to the job's inputs); else null.
input_table.title: Input Table

kind.description: derives: the input's value flows into the output column; filters: it decides which rows appear (WHERE, JOIN ON, HAVING, IN=, subsetting IF); ranks: it decides which row survives (ORDER BY in a ROW_NUMBER, NODUPKEY, FIRST./LAST.).
kind.title: Kind

lines.description: Line numbers in the legacy file that show the edge.
lines.title: Lines

output_column.description: The output column the edge feeds; null for an edge that decides which rows appear (a filter) or which row survives (a ranking).
output_column.title: Output Column

output_table.description: The job's output table, schema-qualified, e.g. rpt.claims_summary.
output_table.title: Output Table

transform.description: A few words on the logic, e.g. 'UPPER(RTRIM(lob_code))'.
transform.title: Transform

edges.transform: lob_code of the policy's first row as loaded (NODUPKEY), merged onto every transaction; used as a CLASS grouping key
put(written_eur, premband.) on the policy's first row as loaded; used as a CLASS grouping key
band labels from the premband format, e.g. 'NEGATIVE', '0-249', '1000+', 'UNKNOWN'
n(policy_id) over one row per policy (NODUPKEY), grouped by lob_code and prem_band
n(written_eur): count of non-missing written_eur per lob_code and prem_band
PROC SORT NODUPKEY BY policy_id keeps the first row for each policy
implicit load order decides which duplicate NODUPKEY keeps (the first as loaded)
merge BY policy_id with if t keeps only transactions (match to the policy band)
PROC MEANS CLASS without MISSING drops rows where lob_code is missing

structured_output.notes:
The only input is dw.fact_premium_earned. lob_code and prem_band come from each policy's first row. PROC SORT NODUPKEY keeps the first row it meets for each policy_id, so which row that is depends on the order the rows were loaded. I have taken that load order to be _row_seq, but the code never names that column, so this edge is an inference (confidence 0.55). For the PySpark port, rebuild the first row as ROW_NUMBER over policy_id ordered by _row_seq.

The match on policy_id with `if t` almost never drops a row, because both sides come from the same table. PROC MEANS has no MISSING option, so it drops any row where lob_code or prem_band is missing. prem_band is never missing: the format sends missing written_eur to 'UNKNOWN' (via OTHER).

n_transactions counts only non-missing written_eur values. It is not a row count.

The final merge on lob_code and prem_band is a full match and drops nothing.
